subject: Protracted completions cascade — root cause & exec sync
messages:
From: Aisha Moreno <aisha.moreno@helioncommerce.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@helioncommerce.com>, sre@helioncommerce.com
Date: 2028-09-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sustained slow completions during peak — urgent

Hi Jordan,

We started seeing a rise in 99th percentile completion times yesterday afternoon and it's persisted through the morning peak today. Checkout and address-auto-complete flows are intermittently timing out for ~5–8% of users; errors show as both 504s at our edge and hung completions from your API. We've attached a zipped sample of traces and request headers (helion_slowtraces_0903.zip).

What we can tell so far: 1) token-level processing time spikes at the 80–120 token mark on many requests, 2) backlog of queued requests visible in our instrumented request_id chain, and 3) transient 429s followed by long tail completions rather than outright rejects.

This is customer-impacting for our checkout funnel (approx 18% of revenue traffic during the incident window). Can we get an exec-level sync today? We need ETA for mitigation and whether you can temporarily route Helion to a dedicated pool or a fallback model variant.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Moreno
Head of Product, Helion Commerce
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-03T09:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained slow completions during peak — urgent

Marissa / Ben — looping you in. Aisha reports sustained p99/completion tail and some 429->long-completion behavior. They attached traces.

Initial notes from our on-call Slack (summary):
- Queue depth in dispatcher grew steadily for Helion's tenant between 15:30–18:40 UTC yesterday; concurrent open requests hit tenant cap at ~1,024 concurrently.
- We observed KV-cache churn on large-context sessions (prefixs not reusing cached KV blobs), amplifying per-token cost and per-request duration.
- A small fraction of requests hit a kernel path causing >2x token-generation latency at 80–120 tokens (suspect path selection + attention scheduling).

Immediate asks:
1) Marissa — can your triage team confirm whether we can flip Helion to a dedicated reserved pool (warm nodes) and temporarily lower their concurrency cap to 512 while we patch?
2) Ben — coordinate with Aisha on customer communication and confirm if they're willing to accept a model-size fallback (gpt-medium-ish equivalent) for the hot paths.
3) Laura — do we engage execs for credits if mitigation impacts throughput?

I'll schedule a 30m exec sync for 14:30 PT and paste runbook/more telemetry.

—Jordan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained slow completions during peak — urgent

Jordan — quick triage from ops: we've reproduced the tail in staging with a traffic replay. Key findings: 
- The tenant concurrency cap is hitting the configured soft-limit; preemptive evictions are queuing requests instead of rejecting, which creates a backpressure wave when KV cache misses spike.
- KV cache eviction policy currently uses an LRU window that is too small for Helion's multi-session workflow; churn causes repeated recomputation of large KV pages.
- The kernel-path that degrades at 80–120 tokens is triggered by mixed-precision fallback on certain attention patterns; engineering has a small patch but it needs a canary rollout.

Immediate mitigations proposed (short horizon):
- Flip Helion to a reserved warm pool for 4 hours (fastest win for p99).
- Temporarily lower their concurrency cap to 512 and enable soft-rejects at 450 to avoid request pileup.
- Enable prefix-level KV hotset pinning for their tenant to reduce eviction churn.
- Canary in region us-west-2 with the kernel patch targeting the 80–120 token regression.

I've attached the operational runbook with step-by-step commands and rollback steps (protracted_completions_runbook_v2.pdf). If we can get Helion to accept the model-fallback for non-checkout routes we can avoid a full capacity surge.

Marissa
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Moreno <aisha.moreno@helioncommerce.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@helioncommerce.com>, sre@helioncommerce.com
Date: 2028-09-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained slow completions during peak — urgent

Jordan / team — thanks for the fast response. We're on board with the reserved pool and temporary concurrency limits. Two asks from our side: 
1) Can you confirm estimated impact to throughput if we drop checkout routes to the fallback model? We need numbers to decide traffic slicing.
2) We will need a credit proposal if there is measurable revenue loss during mitigation.

We can join the 14:30 PT sync. Attaching a short run of our production traces (same zip as earlier).

—Aisha
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sustained slow completions during peak — urgent

Forwarding the thread to myself and the commercial execs. Two things I want prior to the sync: 
- A mitigation ETA for each action (reserved pool flip, concurrency cap change, KV pinning, kernel canary). Please provide expected p99 reduction and estimated downtime/risk.
- A recommendation on customer compensation. Suggest we prepare a two-tier offer: (A) one-week service credit equal to 7% of billed usage in the incident window, or (B) deeper credit + technical audit if this recurs.

If ops can move the reserved flip within 2 hours of the sync, we will offer the credit transparently and track impact.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Moreno <aisha.moreno@helioncommerce.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-06T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Protracted completions cascade — exec sync notes and next steps

Thanks everyone for the sync earlier today. Summary & action items: 

What we saw: sustained queueing driven by tenant concurrency cap reach + KV cache churn; a minority kernel path triggered extra per-token latency at ~80–120 tokens. This produced a tail that manifested as a mix of 429s and long-running completions.

Mitigations executed:
- 14:45 PT: Flipped Helion to reserved warm pool (us-west-2) — immediate p95/p99 improvement in the first 10 minutes.
- 15:00 PT: Lowered cap to 512 with soft-reject threshold at 450; this limited accrual and reduced queue depth by ~78% in 30m.
- 15:20 PT: Enabled hotspot KV pinning for Helion tenant.
- 15:35 PT: Canary of kernel patch in region (INF-4829) — monitored for 60m, no regressions; scheduled deploy to remaining canaries.

Customer compensation: Laura proposed a one-week 7% usage credit for the incident window; Ben will confirm exact billing window and dollar figure and share with Helion.

Open items:
- Ops to run a post-incident KV-residency analysis and propose a permanent hotset policy (Owner: Marissa) — ETA 2028-09-10.
- Engineering to validate kernel-path patch across mixed-precision stacks and include guard rails (Owner: INF eng) — ETA 2028-09-12.
- Commercial to finalize credit & comms (Owner: Ben) — ETA 2028-09-05.

Attachments included: protracted_completions_runbook_v2.pdf, mitigation_patch_notes.txt.

If Helion wants a joint technical post-mortem with their SREs we'll schedule one next week.

—Jordan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
